sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This episode explores explicit themes.
sentences.zh: 本期节目探讨的内容较为露骨。

sentences.en: If you're listening with small kids, you may want to save this for later.
sentences.zh: 如果您正带着年幼的孩子收听，建议您稍后再听。

sentences.en: Parties were huge.
sentences.zh: 派对非常盛行。

sentences.en: Hookups were huge.
sentences.zh: 约炮非常盛行。

sentences.en: Everyone just seemed to be doing everything with each other.
sentences.zh: 每个人似乎都在和所有人发生关系。

sentences.en: And yet I always kind of felt like I wasn't doing it right.
sentences.zh: 然而，我总觉得我好像没做对。

sentences.en: There are certain ideas that send the media into a panic.
sentences.zh: 有些观念会让媒体陷入恐慌。

sentences.en: One of them is hookup culture.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是“约炮文化”。

sentences.en: College students are, quote-unquote, hooking up.
sentences.zh: 大学生们，用“引号”来说，正在“约炮”。

sentences.en: Hookup.
sentences.zh: 约炮。

sentences.en: Hookup.
sentences.zh: 约炮。

sentences.en: Hookup.
sentences.zh: 约炮。

sentences.en: Hookup.
sentences.zh: 约炮。

sentences.en: Hookup culture.
sentences.zh: 约炮文化。

sentences.en: Yeah, where people can just be sitting in a cafe and find someone to hook up with.
sentences.zh: 没错，人们坐在咖啡馆里就能找到人约炮。

sentences.en: Are you buying this?
sentences.zh: 你信吗？

sentences.en: Kids are more sexual than ever.
sentences.zh: 现在的孩子比以往任何时候都更早熟。

sentences.en: Stories about casual sex on college campuses have long been a staple of cable news.
sentences.zh: 关于大学校园里随意性行为的故事，长期以来一直是电视新闻的常客。

sentences.en: But the truth is more nuanced.
sentences.zh: 但事实要复杂得多。

sentences.en: College students are actually not having more sex than their parents did a generation ago.
sentences.zh: 事实上，现在的大学生并没有比他们上一代人的性生活更频繁。

sentences.en: But something has changed.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情确实改变了。

sentences.en: Not just in what students do or what they don't do, but in how they think.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是学生们做了什么或没做什么，而是他们的思维方式变了。

sentences.en: I have students who have had sex many times drunk, but have never held someone's hand.
sentences.zh: 我有些学生在醉酒状态下发生过多次性行为，却从未牵过对方的手。

sentences.en: If casual sex was taboo a generation ago, emotional intimacy has become taboo today.
sentences.zh: 如果说上一代人视随意性行为为禁忌，那么今天，情感亲密反而成了禁忌。

sentences.en: It's something to be explored in secret.
sentences.zh: 这成了需要私下探索的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe even something to be ashamed about.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是需要感到羞耻的事情。

sentences.en: I think it feels bad to be used, but I think the alternative is that nobody wants to use you, and I think that that's worse.
sentences.zh: 我觉得被利用感觉很糟糕，但我觉得另一种选择是没人想利用你，而我觉得那更糟糕。

sentences.en: Lisa Wade is a sociologist at Occidental College.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·韦德是西方学院的一名社会学家。

sentences.en: In her book, American Hookup, The New Culture of Sex on Campus, Lisa interviews college students and finds that hookup culture has a complex set of social rules.
sentences.zh: 在她的著作《美国约炮：校园性爱新文化》中，丽莎采访了大学生，发现约炮文化有一套复杂的社会规则。

sentences.en: She says these rules threaten the emotional well-being of students, those who embrace the culture, and those who want nothing to do with it.
sentences.zh: 她说这些规则威胁到了学生的情感健康，无论是那些拥抱这种文化的人，还是那些不想与之有任何瓜葛的人。

sentences.en: Lisa, thanks for joining me on Hidden Brain today.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，感谢你今天参加《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We spoke with several students in your book, Lisa, and we're going to hear from them in this conversation.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，我们采访了你书中的几位学生，在接下来的对话中，我们将听到他们的声音。

sentences.en: One of the things that kept coming up was that there's no one definition of what hooking up actually is.
sentences.zh: 其中一个反复出现的问题是，对于“约炮”到底是什么，并没有一个统一的定义。

sentences.en: It can mean a variety of things, from making out to having sex.
sentences.zh: 它可以指代各种行为，从亲热到发生性关系。

sentences.en: But for all the ambiguity, there does seem to be a clear set of guidelines when it comes to how students should hookup.
sentences.zh: 但尽管存在这种模糊性，在学生们该如何约炮这件事上，似乎确实有一套明确的准则。

sentences.en: You know, it's funny because the ideology around hookups is that they're supposed to be spontaneous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，因为关于约炮的意识形态是它们应该是自发的。

sentences.en: And the fact is that there's a pretty rigid set of rules for how hookups happen.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，对于约炮如何发生，有一套相当僵化的规则。

sentences.en: Many of them, probably most of them, start at parties where there's drinking.
sentences.zh: 其中许多，可能大多数，始于有酒精助兴的派对。

sentences.en: And the way to initiate it is through dancing.
sentences.zh: 而发起的方式是通过跳舞。

sentences.en: And so usually in these heterosexual encounters, women will initiate the dancing by going into the middle of the dance floor and then, in a very sort of gender traditional way,
sentences.zh: 通常在这些异性恋邂逅中，女性会通过走进舞池中央来发起跳舞，然后，以一种非常传统的性别方式，

sentences.en: hope that someone picks her and comes up along behind her.
sentences.zh: 希望有人选中她并走到她身后。

sentences.en: Sometimes the woman doesn't even know who is behind her,
sentences.zh: 有时女性甚至不知道身后是谁，

sentences.en: which creates a conundrum because part of hooking up is trying to hook up with people that your friends approve of and think are like a good catch.
sentences.zh: 这就造成了一个难题，因为约炮的一部分是试图与你的朋友认可、认为是个“好对象”的人约炮。

sentences.en: And so often she's dancing, someone comes up behind her,
sentences.zh: 所以通常她跳着舞，有人走到她身后，

sentences.en: and then what she'll do is she'll look across the circle to one of her girlfriends and try to get some indication as to whether or not she should continue.
sentences.zh: 然后她会做的是看向圈子里的某个女性朋友，试图得到某种暗示，看看她是否应该继续。

sentences.en: Let's talk some more about this idea that hookups are a way to win the approval of your friends.
sentences.zh: 我们再来谈谈这个观点，即约炮是赢得朋友认可的一种方式。

sentences.en: You're saying that some hookups move you up the social pecking order and others move you down?
sentences.zh: 你是说有些约炮能让你在社交等级中上升，而另一些则让你下降？

sentences.en: Hookups are decidedly not about finding any sort of romantic connection and suggesting that it should be or that one is doing it for that reason is tantamount to breaking a social rule.
sentences.zh: 约炮绝对不是为了寻找任何形式的浪漫联系，暗示它应该是这样，或者有人是为了这个原因才去约炮，等同于打破社会规则。

sentences.en: They're often not so much about pleasure, in particular for women.
sentences.zh: 它们往往与快乐无关，尤其是对女性而言。

sentences.en: They're very much about status.
sentences.zh: 它们更多是关于地位。

sentences.en: So the idea is to be able to brag about or having sort of gotten someone who other people might also wish they could have gotten.
sentences.zh: 所以其理念是能够吹嘘，或者说搞定了其他人也想搞定的人。

sentences.en: So it's all about being able to say, I got that guy over there or that person that everyone's looking for.
sentences.zh: 所以重点在于能够说：我搞定了那边的那个家伙，或者那个每个人都在寻找的人。

sentences.en: I managed to be the one who hooked up with him tonight.
sentences.zh: 我今晚成功地成为了和他约炮的那个人。

sentences.en: One of the unspoken rules you talk about in hookup culture is that it's really important that the hookup be meaningless.
sentences.zh: 你在约炮文化中谈到的潜规则之一是，约炮必须是“毫无意义的”，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: One of the young men we spoke with described a situation that almost seems Kafka-esque.
sentences.zh: 我们采访的一位年轻男性描述了一种几乎像是卡夫卡式的情境。

sentences.en: We really liked each other, but she would not have sex with me.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很喜欢彼此，但她不愿和我发生性关系。

sentences.en: But I also knew that she was hooking up with someone.
sentences.zh: 但我同时也知道她正在和别人约炮。

sentences.en: And this was such a confusing concept, which is that people will have sex with people that they don't like, but won't have sex with people that they do like.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人困惑的概念，即人们会和不喜欢的人发生性关系，却不愿和喜欢的人发生性关系。

sentences.en: And of course, what this young man is saying, he can't understand why this young woman who likes him and that he likes is having sex with someone else whom she doesn't like,
sentences.zh: 当然，这位年轻人所说的是，他不明白为什么这个喜欢他、他也喜欢的年轻女性会和另一个她不喜欢的人发生性关系，

sentences.en: but won't have sex with him.
sentences.zh: 却不愿和他发生性关系。

sentences.en: What the students are confronted with is this artificial binary between careless and careful sex.
sentences.zh: 学生们所面对的是这种在“粗心性爱”和“小心性爱”之间的人为二元对立。

sentences.en: On the one hand, we have this idea that when we get into romantic relationships, we're supposed to be loving and kind.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我们有一种观念，即当我们进入恋爱关系时，我们应该充满爱意和善意。

sentences.en: And the sex that happens in those kinds of relationships is very committed.
sentences.zh: 而那种关系中发生的性行为是非常忠诚的。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, we have this concept of casual sex, which is the opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们有“随意性行为”这个概念，它是前者的对立面。

sentences.en: And that means that all of the kindnesses that go along with romantic relationships are considered off-script once casual sex is on the table.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一旦随意性行为摆上台面，恋爱关系中所有的善意都被视为“不合剧本”。

sentences.en: So if two students are going to hook up together and they want it to be meaningless,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果两个学生要约炮，并且他们希望这毫无意义，

sentences.en: then they have to do some work to make sure that both they and everyone else understands that we're over in this meaningless camp and not this powerfully meaningful one.
sentences.zh: 那么他们必须做些工作，确保他们自己和所有其他人都明白，我们是在这个“毫无意义”的阵营，而不是那个“意义重大”的阵营。

sentences.en: And so to sort of convince themselves and other people or to show themselves and other people that it was meaningless, they have to find a way to perform meaningless.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了说服自己和他人，或者向自己和他人展示这是毫无意义的，他们必须找到一种方式来“表演”这种毫无意义。

sentences.en: It's not automatic.
sentences.zh: 这不是自动发生的。

sentences.en: And they do that by, for example, making sure that they're drunk or they appear to be drunk when they hook up.
sentences.zh: 他们通过例如确保自己喝醉了，或者在约炮时表现得像喝醉了来做到这一点。

sentences.en: So my students actually speak in pretty hushed tones about sober sex.
sentences.zh: 所以我的学生们在谈论清醒状态下的性行为时，声音压得很低。

sentences.en: Sober sex is very serious.
sentences.zh: 清醒性爱是非常严肃的。

sentences.en: But if the students have been drinking, then that helps send the message that it's meaningless.
sentences.zh: 但如果学生们喝了酒，那就有助于传达这毫无意义的信息。

sentences.en: Another way is to make sure that they don't hook up with the same person very many times.
sentences.zh: 另一种方式是确保他们不会和同一个人约炮太多次。

sentences.en: So if they really don't like the person in a romantic way, just hook up once, maybe twice, and then cut it off.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们真的在浪漫层面上不喜欢那个人，就约一次，最多两次，然后就断掉。

sentences.en: And then the third thing they have to do to try to establish this meaninglessness is to sort of give that person a demotion in their lives afterward.
sentences.zh: 第三件他们必须做的事，就是试图在事后给那个人在他们的生活中“降级”。

sentences.en: The idea that it's meaningless means that we're also not supposed to care about that person at all and in any way.
sentences.zh: “毫无意义”这个概念意味着我们也不应该以任何方式关心那个人。

sentences.en: You talk in the book about how even though, you know, talk about hookups is ubiquitous on college campuses, that doesn't necessarily reflect how much of it is actually going on.
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到，尽管约炮在大学校园里无处不在，但这并不一定反映了实际发生的频率。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of consternation about students' sexual activity.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对学生的性行为有很多担忧。

sentences.en: But it turns out that they are no more sexually active by most measures than their parents were at their age.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，从大多数衡量标准来看，他们并不比他们父母在那个年纪时更活跃。

sentences.en: The average graduating senior has hooked up eight times in four years.
sentences.zh: 普通毕业生在四年里约炮八次。

sentences.en: So that's once a semester.
sentences.zh: 也就是每学期一次。

sentences.en: And half of those hookups are with someone that they've hooked up with before.
sentences.zh: 而且其中一半的约炮对象是他们之前约过的人。

sentences.en: And in fact, about a third of students won't hook up even a single time their entire college career.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大约三分之一的学生在整个大学生涯中一次都不会约炮。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that they're not surrounded by these really powerful ideas about what they should be doing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他们没有被这些关于他们“应该做什么”的强大观念所包围。

sentences.en: And it doesn't mean that they can change how their peers interact with them or the way in which higher education works.
sentences.zh: 这也不意味着他们能改变同龄人与他们互动的方式，或者高等教育运作的方式。

sentences.en: So even though campus hookup culture might actually be something that is endorsed by a relatively small number of people who are enthusiasts,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管校园约炮文化可能实际上是由少数热衷者所支持的，

sentences.en: one of the points you make is that these are people who often come from groups who have traditionally had a lot of power and privilege in society.
sentences.zh: 你提出的观点之一是，这些人往往来自在社会中传统上拥有大量权力和特权的群体。

sentences.en: About 15% of students really, really, truly enjoy hookup culture.
sentences.zh: 大约15%的学生真的、真的、非常享受约炮文化。

sentences.en: It gives them exactly what they want out of college.
sentences.zh: 这给了他们想要从大学中得到的一切。

sentences.en: And studies show that if you ask those students, and they're the students that are hooking up the most,
sentences.zh: 研究表明，如果你问那些学生，而且他们正是约炮最频繁的学生，

sentences.en: if you ask them if they're having a good time, they say yes.
sentences.zh: 如果你问他们是否玩得开心，他们会说是的。

sentences.en: And I believe them.
sentences.zh: 我相信他们。

sentences.en: About a third of students are completely opted out.
sentences.zh: 大约三分之一的学生完全选择不参与。

sentences.en: The rest of the students are somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 其余的学生处于中间地带。

sentences.en: And they're ambivalent about the idea of casual sex.
sentences.zh: 他们对随意性行为的观念持矛盾态度。

sentences.en: But if you look at the students who enjoy hookup culture the most,
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看那些最享受约炮文化的学生，

sentences.en: those students are disproportionately going to be heterosexual, white, come from an upper middle class or wealthy background.
sentences.zh: 这些学生不成比例地是异性恋、白人、来自中上阶层或富裕背景。

sentences.en: They're going to be male.
sentences.zh: 他们通常是男性。

sentences.en: They're going to be able-bodied, conventionally attractive.
sentences.zh: 他们身体健全，外貌符合传统审美。

sentences.en: And how is this different for racial minorities or people from the LGBT community?
sentences.zh: 那么这对少数族裔或LGBT群体有什么不同呢？

sentences.en: Racial minorities face all kinds of complicated problems that white students don't.
sentences.zh: 少数族裔面临着白人学生所没有的各种复杂问题。

sentences.en: And it depends a lot kind of on what particular intersection we're looking at.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上取决于我们所观察的具体交叉点。

sentences.en: So some racial minorities are embraced by white students more than others.
sentences.zh: 有些少数族裔比其他人更容易被白人学生接纳。

sentences.en: So African-American men and Asian women are usually considered hot and exotic,
sentences.zh: 例如，非裔美国男性和亚裔女性通常被认为很火辣、很有异国情调，

sentences.en: whereas Asian men and African-American women are considered less so.
sentences.zh: 而亚裔男性和非裔美国女性则被认为没那么有吸引力。

sentences.en: So it very much depends kind of on what intersection of race and gender and class, too, that students are sitting in.
sentences.zh: 所以这很大程度上取决于学生所处的种族、性别和阶级的交叉点。

sentences.en: But overall, we see lower rates of hooking up among racial minorities for both push and pull reasons.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，由于推力和拉力原因，我们看到少数族裔的约炮率较低。

sentences.en: So part of it is they're pushed out because of racism and an erotic hierarchy that privileges whiteness.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他们因为种族主义和一种将白人特权化的色情等级制度而被排挤出去。

sentences.en: But they also tend to get pulled out because racial minorities are more likely to be religious.
sentences.zh: 但他们也倾向于被拉出来，因为少数族裔更有可能信教。

sentences.en: They drink less alcohol.
sentences.zh: 他们饮酒较少。

sentences.en: They maybe had to be more squeaky clean to get into college to begin with.
sentences.zh: 他们可能为了进入大学本身就必须表现得更加洁身自好。

sentences.en: So racial minorities aren't as welcome in hookup culture.
sentences.zh: 所以少数族裔在约炮文化中并不那么受欢迎。

sentences.en: And they also don't find it as attractive.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也觉得这种文化没那么吸引人。

sentences.en: And what about the LGBT community?
sentences.zh: 那LGBT群体呢？

sentences.en: For students who don't identify as heterosexual, and we actually still need to do more research on this,
sentences.zh: 对于那些不认同自己是异性恋的学生，我们实际上还需要对此进行更多研究，

sentences.en: but what seems to be happening is that on small campuses or campuses where people aren't very out,
sentences.zh: 但似乎发生的情况是，在小型校园或人们不太出柜的校园里，

sentences.en: there's not an alternative hookup scene for students who don't identify as heterosexual or bisexual.
sentences.zh: 对于不认同自己是异性恋或双性恋的学生来说，没有替代的约炮场景。

sentences.en: And the hookup scene that does exist is hyper-heterosexualized.
sentences.zh: 而现有的约炮场景是高度异性恋化的。

sentences.en: And in those cases, students participate at their own risk, risking homophobia in either behavior or attitude,
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下，学生们是在冒着风险参与，冒着在行为或态度上遭遇恐同的风险，

sentences.en: or they go off campus.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会去校外。

sentences.en: And that is why Grindr hit college campuses way earlier than Tinder did,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么Grindr比Tinder更早进入大学校园的原因，

sentences.en: because a lot of students who identified as non-heterosexual were using it to find hookups off campus.
sentences.zh: 因为许多认同自己是非异性恋的学生都在用它在校外寻找约炮对象。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask Lisa about the effects of hookup culture on the emotional lives of young people.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我要问丽莎关于约炮文化对年轻人情感生活的影响。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: One argument that some make, and this includes feminists on the left and libertarians on the right,
sentences.zh: 有些人提出了一个论点，这包括左翼的女权主义者和右翼的自由意志主义者，

sentences.en: is that hookups can be liberating.
sentences.zh: 即约炮可以是解放性的。

sentences.en: People have a chance to experiment, try new things.
sentences.zh: 人们有机会去实验，去尝试新事物。
